afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 262326
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
Issued by National Weather Service Tucson AZ
426 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and tranquil weather conditions will continue through the
  middle of the week with temperatures within a few degrees of 
  daily normals.

- An unsettled weather pattern will return to the region late in
  the week and persist through this weekend resulting in much 
  cooler temperatures and chances for widespread rainfall.

- There will also be a possibility of embedded thunderstorms with
  heavier rainfall which could lead to localized flash flooding 
  Friday and Sunday. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
Latest mid-lvl wv imagery and 500 mb streamline analysis reveals 
a trough of low pressure located over the Pac NW along with a 
weak shortwave progressing through the Intermountain West. This 
disturbance will result in a few high clouds passing through N AZ 
this afternoon, otherwise dry and tranquil weather conditions are 
anticipated across our forecast area during the next 24 hrs. Under
mostly clear skies, temperatures will remain within a degree or 
two of seasonal normals with highs reaching the mid 80s across the
lower deserts and the mid to upper 70s for the higher elevations.
Due to calm winds and dry conditions overnight, cool overnight 
low temperatures in the mid 50s to around 60 degrees can be 
expected Tuesday morning.

Quiet weather conditions will continue into the middle of the week 
under quasi-zonal westerly flow aloft. Dry air aloft will help 
keep skies clear to mostly clear through Tuesday before a slight 
shift in the upper level winds out of the southwest helps to draw 
more abundant high clouds into our region. Overall there will be 
very little variation in 500 mb heights which will result in 
daytime highs topping out in the mid 80s across the lower deserts.
Overnight lows will also fall within a normal range in the mid 
50s to lower 60s through Wednesday. 

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/... 
The weather pattern is expected to shift late this week with a deep 
trough getting carved out over the Pacific Northwest and southwest 
to off the coast of California by Thursday. The polar jet associated 
with the northern stream system is expected to dip farther southward 
off the West Coast, while a stronger subtropical jet across the 
central Pacific shifts eastward toward Baja. Although these jet 
branches are not expected to phase together going into Friday, there 
is likely to be some combined energy reaching the Western U.S. 

As the trough sets up to our west on Wednesday into Thursday, high 
level moisture will stream into our region, followed by increasing 
southerly moist flow in the lower levels Thursday night into Friday. 
Guidance is in very good agreement southerly low level moist 
advection will combine with some top-down saturation in the upper 
levels on Friday across southern and central Arizona. PWATs are 
shown to quickly rise to just above 200% of normal by Friday 
morning, while low level mixing ratios rise to a respectable 8-9 
g/kg. This decent moisture is also expected to coincide with modest 
low level upslope forcing and quite strong mid and upper level 
ascent within the left exit region of the subtropical jet. Although 
we are still four days out, confidence is quite good in shower 
activity blossoming at some point Thursday night/Friday morning 
across south-central Arizona and lasting through much of Friday. 
Guidance also shows modest MUCAPE of 250-500 J/kg on Friday which 
should allow for some isolated to scattered weak thunderstorms. 
Shear values look to be on the low side, so at this point we are not 
anticipating any strong storms. Forecast QPF from Thursday night 
through Friday night currently averages around 0.50" across the 
Phoenix area to upwards of 0.75-1.00" in the higher terrain north of 
Phoenix. The higher end of guidance is at least double that, so it's 
not out of the question to have to worry about some minor flooding 
issues Friday. WPC has also included this area in a Slight Risk on 
their Day 5 ERO.

The Friday weather event will not be the last period of rain 
expected over the next week as another likely even stronger system 
is forecast to track east northeastward toward southern California 
and northern Baja on Saturday before moving through our region on 
Sunday. There is much more uncertainty with this second weather 
system compared to the first as there are notable timing and 
evolution differences. There are also some differences with the 
potential phasing of the polar and subtropical jet streams which if 
it occurs would likely result in a decent low pressure system 
developing within the base of the large scale trough. Models at 
least agree that there will be as much if not better moisture then 
the Friday system and stronger mid-level and frontal ascent. Given 
the uncertainty, QPF amounts are still quite volatile to any big 
changes in the strength of the system and track. However, so far 
ensemble mean QPF amounts indicate overall higher average amounts 
compared to Friday's event, as well as more widespread coverage. 
Rain chances could also extend into Monday, especially across 
eastern portions of Arizona.

Temperatures will take a hit later this week and through the weekend 
with NBM forecast highs dropping into a 75-80 degree range Friday 
and Saturday and even lower starting Sunday. The coolest air so far 
this fall should move in with the Sunday weather system as highs may 
fall to as the upper 60s to lower 70s for Sunday and Monday. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2300Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:

No aviation weather concerns under mostly clear skies can be expected 
throughout the TAF period. The overall wind pattern will continue
to exhibit the typical diurnal tendencies with speeds generally 
aob 6 kts along with extended periods of light variability to even
calm conditions. A period of light southerly crosswinds is likely
early Tuesday afternoon before the westerly transition by the 
late afternoon hours. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

No aviation weather concerns under mostly clear skies can be
expected throughout the TAF period. Extended periods of light 
variability to even calm conditions are likely with a trend 
towards a light westerly component this evening through the 
overnight hours at KIPL. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Warm and dry conditions will transpire through much of this week 
before a much cooler and wetter pattern sets up Friday into this 
weekend. Minimum humidity levels will continue to fall, reaching 
20-35% today and 15-30% Tuesday before gradual moisture 
improvement arrives mid-week. Overnight recoveries will remain 
good at 40-65%. Winds will remain light each day favoring typical 
diurnal patterns and minimal upslope breeziness.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Salerno
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...Lojero
FIRE WEATHER...Salerno
